evidenceAudit.scope: Adults living with overweight or obesity: measurement, risk assessment (including lower BMI thresholds for Middle Eastern people), behavioural interventions, medicines and referral. Verified against NICE NG246 (2025), the Saudi PHA Clinical Preventive Guideline 2023 and the Saudi Diabetes CPG; doses from FDA labels.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.

pathophysiology.summary: Obesity is excess adiposity that harms health. Central (visceral) fat carries the most cardiometabolic risk, and people of Middle Eastern background develop risk at a lower BMI (NICE NG246).
keyMechanisms: Energy intake exceeding expenditure over time, shaped by genes, environment, sleep, medicines and psychology.
Visceral fat drives insulin resistance, dyslipidaemia, hypertension and fatty liver.
Weight loss of 5–10% improves blood pressure, glucose and joint symptoms.

symptoms: Weight gain; breathlessness, snoring, joint pain, low mood.
physicalSigns: BMI; waist circumference; acanthosis nigricans; signs of comorbidities.
redFlags: Rapid unexplained weight gain — consider endocrine causes
Sleep apnoea symptoms with daytime sleepiness

ruleIn.modalityTarget: BMI/waist every 2 years in adults (PHA); waist-to-height if BMI below 35 (NICE)
ruleIn.expectedFinding: BMI 25–29.9 overweight; 30–34.9 class 1; 35–39.9 class 2; 40+ class 3. Middle Eastern background: overweight 23–27.4, obesity 27.5+ (NICE). Waist-to-height 0.5 or more = central adiposity.
ruleIn.normalValue: BMI 18.5–24.9 (23 for Middle Eastern background); waist-to-height below 0.5

clinicalManagement.title: Assess sensitively
actions: Ask permission before discussing weight; address presenting problems first (NICE NG246).

clinicalManagement.title: Behavioural interventions
actions: Refer adults with BMI 30 or more to intensive multicomponent behavioural interventions (PHA footnote 3).
Reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity (NICE).

clinicalManagement.title: Medicines
clinicalManagement.timeframe: After lifestyle is started and evaluated
actions: Options (NICE NG246 Table 1): tirzepatide, semaglutide, liraglutide (specialist services, per TAs), orlistat (BMI 30+, or 28+ with risk factors).
Use thresholds 2.5 kg/m² lower for Middle Eastern background for GLP-1-based medicines (NICE).
All medicines alongside diet and activity; avoid in pregnancy.

clinicalManagement.title: Surgery
actions: Refer for bariatric assessment if BMI 40+, or 35–39.9 with a significant comorbidity (lower by 2.5 for Middle Eastern background) — see Bariatric topic.

learningObjectives: Assess overweight and obesity and offer tiered treatment.

keyPoints: Use lower BMI thresholds for Middle Eastern people.
Refer for surgery at BMI 40+ (or 35+ with comorbidity).
pitfalls: Using standard BMI cut-offs for Middle Eastern patients.

patientEducation: Any weight loss helps; aim for sustainable change.
lifestyleAndDiet: Reduced-calorie, healthy eating pattern; 150 min/week activity; sleep.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review weight, comorbidities and medicines regularly; stop orlistat if inadequate response per product information.
